title: Integral models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. All schemes below are Noetherian schemes in this setting. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\cO_E$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, and residue field $\kappa_E=\cO_E/\pi_E$. Fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Write $C_X=(\cO_E)_X$ for the constant coefficient sheaf and $R_X=\cO_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\cO_E}\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ for the completed coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Write $D_R(X)=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},R_X)$ and $D_C(X)=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},C_X)$ for the derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The categories $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ mean bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and their full subcategory of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]; derived completeness means that the canonical map to the derived limit of the reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$ is an isomorphism [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. For constant coefficients use the same condition with $C_X$.

Let $\Dc(X,\cO_E)\subset D_C(X)$ consist of derived $\pi_E$-complete complexes $L$ for which $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{C_X}(\kappa_E)_X$ has constructible cohomology pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and finite Tor dimension. This is the constant-coefficient category of [det-lem-integral-models-stacks]. Then $\Dctf(X,\cO_E)=\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and the following hold.

1. Restriction of scalars along $C_X\to R_X$ gives an equivalence between the derived $\pi_E$-complete objects of $D_R(X)$ and those of $D_C(X)$.
2. For $K\in D_R(X)$, $K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ if and only if $\operatorname{Res}K\in\Dc(X,\cO_E)$. Equivalently, $K$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ precisely when it is derived complete and $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}(\kappa_E)_X$ is a bounded constructible complex pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$.
3. The categories $\Dbc(-,\cO_E)$ are preserved by the inverse image $f^*$ for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in the setting, by $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}-$, and by $a_!=i_*u_!$ for every locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow X$, with $u$ open and $i$ closed. The inverse image and tensor functors are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; open extension by zero is [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].
4. Every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained by finitely many cones and shifts from objects $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$, where $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally closed and $L_0$ is a lisse finite free $\cO_{E,S}$-module, meaning a module pro-étale locally isomorphic to a finite free coefficient module. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is obtained in the same way from objects $\QbarX\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ for one finite subextension $E\subset\Qlb$ depending on the object; here $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$ uses [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Moreover $a_!L_0\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and for every $n\ge1$ its derived reduction is $a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$, a bounded constructible complex with coefficients $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$.

proof.text: Specialize [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) to $\Lambda=\cO_E$. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ choose an interval $[r,s]$ containing its cohomology; the cited statement gives Tor amplitude in $[r-1,s]$. Thus $K\in\Dctf(X,\cO_E)$. The reverse inclusion is part of the definition, and both are full subcategories of the same derived category, so they are equal.

source.place: clauses (2) and the definition of finite Tor amplitude; realizes the opening equality of the item

proof.text: By [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients](1), the canonical map $C_X\to R_X$ is flat and identifies the quotients modulo every $\pi_E^n$. Its clause (2) says exactly that restriction of scalars is an equivalence on derived complete objects, with inverse given by extension of scalars followed by derived completion. This proves (1). Its clause (3) also identifies the reductions of a completed-coefficient complex before and after restriction of scalars; we will use that identification in the criterion below.

source.place: clauses (1)-(3); the item proof, first paragraph, uses Stacks 099L and 099I

proof.text: Apply [det-lem-integral-models-stacks] to the Noetherian scheme $X$ and the given finite extension $E$. Its displayed equivalence is $K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ if and only if $\operatorname{Res}K\in\Dc(X,\cO_E)$, proving the first assertion of (2). Its definition of $\Dc$ is in the constant-coefficient category $D_C(X)$, so no identification of the two ambient coefficient categories is being made.

source.place: displayed equivalence; item proof, first paragraph

proof.text: For clarity, over a constant field sheaf every module sheaf is flat. Indeed view such a sheaf $N$ as a presheaf of vector spaces over the constant presheaf $\kappa_E$. For each object $U$, tensoring with $N(U)$ preserves finite limits: choose a basis, so this tensor functor is a direct sum of copies of the identity on vector spaces. Limits of presheaves are objectwise. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat] to this presheaf and to the constant presheaf of rings. Their sheafifications are $N$ and $(\kappa_E)_X$, respectively. This proves the flatness assertion on either site without assuming geometric points of the pro-étale topos.

source.place: Tag 03ET, lemma-flatness-sheafification; explicit field specialization of the item proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Consequently a bounded-cohomology complex $B$ over $(\kappa_E)_X$ has finite Tor dimension. Choose a representing complex and an interval $[r,s]$ outside which its cohomology vanishes. The good truncation at $r$ replaces the degree-$r$ term by its incoming cokernel, and the good truncation at $s$ replaces the degree-$s$ term by its outgoing kernel; the resulting complex is quasi-isomorphic to $B$ and has terms only in $[r,s]$. Every term is flat by the preceding step. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] it is K-flat, so [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] computes its derived tensor with any module sheaf by the ordinary tensor complex, still in $[r,s]$. Conversely finite Tor dimension forces bounded cohomology by testing against the unit module $(\kappa_E)_X$. Thus finite Tor dimension and boundedness are equivalent here.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; the field finite-Tor assertion in the item proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Unpack the definition of $\Dc$ in [det-lem-integral-models-stacks]. By the preceding field calculation its reduction condition is precisely bounded constructibility, with classical cohomology. For $K$ over $R_X$, [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients](3) identifies its reduction modulo $\pi_E$ with that of $\operatorname{Res}K$. Completeness is also equivalent: specialize [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to $A=\cO_E$ and $I=(\pi_E)$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. It identifies the derived limits of the finite reductions and their completion units under restriction of scalars. Restriction detects isomorphisms because it leaves underlying cohomology sheaves unchanged. Thus one completion unit is an isomorphism exactly when the other is. This uses the actual completion units for arbitrary $K$, rather than inferring reflection of completeness merely from an equivalence on the complete subcategories. Finally [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] identifies bounded constructible pro-étale complexes over the discrete Noetherian ring $\kappa_E$ with complexes pulled back from the étale site; $X$ is qcqs since it is Noetherian. Substituting these conditions into the equivalence proved in step 3 gives the second assertion of (2), including both implications of the integral criterion.

source.place: first paragraph, with the missing sk-prop-integral-criterion reference replaced by the comparison statement and the explicit field calculation

proof.text: For (3), [det-lem-integral-models-operations](1) applies to the Noetherian source and target of any given $f:X\to Y$, and yields $f^*K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ for $K\in\Dbc(Y,\cO_E)$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1), the coefficient comparison is an isomorphism and this module inverse image is exact. Thus the $f^*$ in the operations statement is the ambient derived inverse image appearing in (3).

For $K,M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ use [det-lem-integral-models-operations](2). It asserts that the ordinary ambient derived tensor $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}M$, with no subsequent completion, lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$. This is exactly the tensor assertion of (3). The finite-stratification dévissage and projection formula are encapsulated in this existing operations lemma, rather than asserted as an uncited fact about restrictions.

For a locally closed immersion factor $a=i\circ u$ as in the statement. All three schemes are Noetherian and $u$ is quasi-compact. Clause (3) of [det-lem-integral-models-operations] states that $a_!L=i_*u_!L\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ for every $L\in\Dbc(S,\cO_E)$. This proves the remaining preservation assertion in (3).

source.place: clause (3); item proof, Extension by zero

proof.text: For (4), take the class $\mathcal G_E$ in [det-lem-integral-models-generators]. By its definition the generators are exactly $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$ for the locally closed immersions and lisse finite free lattices in the assertion. Its clause (1) says that every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ belongs to the closure under finitely many cones and shifts of this class. This proves the $E$-coefficient generation assertion.

source.place: definition of G_E and clause (1); item proof, last paragraph

proof.text: For $\Qlb$-coefficients use clause (2) of [det-lem-integral-models-generators], with its explicitly defined class $\mathcal G_{\Qlb}$. It states generation by finitely many cones and shifts with one finite subextension $E$ for the given object. Its generators are precisely $\QbarX\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ as written in (4). The tensor here is the ambient scalar-extension tensor of the source statement.

source.place: definition of G_Qlb and clause (2); item proof, last paragraph, finite coefficient descent

proof.text: Finally clause (3) of [det-lem-integral-models-generators] states both $a_!L_0\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ and, for every $n\ge1$, the equality of derived reduction with $a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$ and its membership in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$, coming from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$. These are all the remaining assertions of (4); the reduction is derived, including at $n=1$, and the same chosen $a,L_0$ is used for every $n$.

source.place: clause (3); item proof, last paragraph, classical torsion reductions

proof_origin.place: first paragraph and the three operations and generator paragraphs; existing detailed blueprint statements reused; field finite-Tor assertion made explicit using Stacks 03ET and 06YQ

tool_uses.why: Generic coefficient-completion comparison identifies finite-reduction derived limits and their units, which is needed to reflect completeness for arbitrary complexes, not just to compare the complete subcategories.
Existing general integral/rational Tor-amplitude theorem supplies the introductory DVR equality; it follows the same finite constant local-model argument.
Generic flat sheafification theorem supplies the omitted justification that all modules over the constant residue field sheaf are flat.
Generic K-flatness theorem justifies computing derived tensor by the bounded complex of flat residue-field sheaves.
